notes.2: Candidates should take care to read the full question. Many candidates selected option B, which contained a substance with the largest Rf value but did not recognise that this sample was impure.
notes.4: This question discriminated between candidates. Some candidates chose option D. This suggests candidates were adding rather than subtracting one electron when counting the electrons in a sodium ion.
notes.6: Candidates are required to be able to draw dot-and-cross diagrams for substances such as methanol. A quickly sketched diagram would have helped candidates. Some candidates appeared to be guessing.
notes.11: Most candidates identified the neutralisation reaction. Confusion was shown between the terms endothermic and exothermic with option C being the most common incorrect answer.
notes.13: Most candidates answered this correctly although some selected option C. The effect of pressure on the position of equilibrium was less well understood than the effect of temperature.
notes.21: This was one of the more demanding questions on the paper with the majority of candidates choosing option A. This suggests that most candidates recall the trend in density of elements in Group VII but are less secure in their recall of the trend in density of elements in Group I.
notes.25: Option C was a common incorrect answer. Candidates should take care to read the whole statement. Although potassium does react with water to form hydrogen, candidates should recall that alkali metals form alkaline solutions, not acidic ones.
notes.27: Common incorrect choices were options B or C. It should be recalled that hydrogen is not found in clean dry air and so it cannot be extracted from air.
notes.31: Most candidates narrowed their choice to either options B or C. Many thought that the formation of oleum required a catalyst and selected option C.
notes.34: Questions on the nomenclature and structure of esters discriminate well between candidates. Overall, the distribution of answers suggests that some candidates were guessing.
notes.40: Options C was chosen by some candidates, suggesting that the presence of nitrogen in an amide bond is not known by all candidates. Option D was also a common incorrect choice.
notes.general_comments: Candidates performed very well on this paper. Most questions were answered correctly by at least half of the candidates. Questions 1, 7, 8, 16 and 28 were found to be least challenging. Candidates found Questions 21 and 39 the most challenging.
